target_customer: Live event promoters, venues and festivals that sell tickets and need fan marketing
problem: Event marketers lacked a tool that ties email, SMS and ads to ticket sales data from ticketing platforms.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for event marketing, integrated with ticketing platforms

founders.name: Ian Roberts
education: University of Waterloo, student at founding
founders.background_notes: Described by BetaKit as a student in a University of Waterloo computer lab when Hive began.

founders.name: Patrick Hannigan
education: University of Waterloo, student at founding

technical_complexity.rationale: Initial product was a ticketing app built by two students; the later marketing product needs integrations with ticketing platforms, which is standard SaaS engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Integrations with 40 plus ticketing partners and fan data add switching costs, but marketing tools are copyable.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows an incumbent absorbing Hive; Ticketmaster named it a marketing partner and it stayed independent.

market_need_then: In 2014 the idea was a ticketing business; the marketing need for venues emerged later, with product-market fit found around 2019 per BetaKit. No 2014 demand data found.

branding.domain_note: Uses hive.co, not hive.com; hive.com belongs to a different project management company.

rebrands.why: Company said growth from ticketing into event marketing prompted the refresh.

brand_strength.rationale: Generic word shared with several other Hive companies and no sourced brand pull; recognition within live events is through Ticketmaster partnership and press.

pivots.to: Engagement and analytics tools for musicians
Marketing software for music venues and event marketers
pivots.why: BetaKit says product-market fit came around 2019

outcome_analysis: Hive began in 2014 as a student ticketing startup, pivoted several times and found product-market fit around 2019 with marketing software for live event organizers. It lost 60 percent of its revenue when COVID-19 hit but avoided layoffs because it was profitable. By 2026 it served over a thousand venues and raised a mostly secondary 27 million dollar Series B, so it is a durable, modest-capital company.
notes: Total raised about 35M USD mostly secondary per BetaKit. Series B was majority secondary buying out Avenue Growth; the primary amount is not disclosed. Seed date is 2014 with no month. Aggregators (startupintros, one claiming 120K total) conflict and are ignored. Search coverage for hive.com (project management) is a different company. Education: only 'University of Waterloo students', degrees not stated. COVID revenue loss of 60 percent and no layoffs per press summary. No competitor named in dated sources near 2014; a Waterloo Velocity article about Eventist ticketing was not opened and no link to Hive is established.
